To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
stem cells can improve function after stroke in the brain by paracrine mechanisms, without acting as a tissue substitute, and by exclusively reactivating the original representation fields.
stem cells are effective in improving functional outcome in a delayed fashion and that this improvement is not due to tissue replacement, but due to paracrine effects of the grafted stem cell.
stem cell mediated functional recovery occurs without stem cell tissue replacement of necrotic tissue and that functional recovery is due to paracrine effects of the grafted stem cell.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a novel mechanism of functional improvement in stroke, which is not based on tissue replacement, but on paracrine effects of the implanted stem cells, which are able to induce functional improvement by activating the original representation fields.
the mechanisms underlying the stem cell-mediated functional improvement after stroke.
the understanding of the functional improvement of the original target field after stroke by stem cell grafting and with the mechanisms of this functional improvement.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
functional recovery after stroke in the rodent model is not due to reorganization, but due to the stem cell mediated restitution of the original function in the original target field.

the stem cells grafted after stroke do not act by tissue replacement or by reorganization, but by reactivating the original representation field by paracrine mechanisms, thus, by a mechanism of functional improvement.

functional recovery by stem cell grafting after ischemic stroke in the rat is due to paracrine effects, which may be mediated by neurotrophic factors, and is not related to a replacement of the lost tissue by the stem cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
stem cells are not a tissue replacement for damaged tissue, but that they can be used for the functional recovery after stroke by a paracrine effect.
the functional improvement is not a result of tissue replacement, but is mediated by a paracrine mechanism of the stem cells.
stem cell therapy for stroke may not be expected to replace tissue but rather to improve function by paracrine mechanisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that

stem cell grafting can be used to promote functional recovery after stroke, and that this functional improvement can occur without stem cell tissue replacement and without clear contribution from reorganization processes.
stem cells are able to improve functional deficits in a chronic stroke model by paracrine effects.
stem cell mediated improvement is not only a short term phenomenon but may last for a long period of time.
